skill.name: full-stack-orchestration-full-stack-feature
skill.description: Coordinates full-stack feature delivery across architecture, implementation, testing, security, deployment, observability, and performance phases.
skill.summary: Orchestrate contract-driven full-stack features from database design through production rollout.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All seven static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code around a resource path and configuration names. The skill contains no shell execution instructions or semantic security threats.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks format a documentation path as Markdown inline code. The line only tells the agent to open a resource and contains no shell command or execution syntax.
The backticks format the stack configuration key as Markdown inline code. The line describes accepted technology-stack input and does not execute a command.
The backticks format the deployment_target configuration key as Markdown inline code. The text lists cloud deployment choices without invoking a shell.
The backticks format the feature_flags configuration key as Markdown inline code. The line documents an enablement option and has no executable content.
The backticks format the api_style configuration key as Markdown inline code. REST and GraphQL are listed as input choices, not shell operations.
The backticks format the testing_depth configuration key as Markdown inline code. The line only documents two testing levels and cannot execute a command.
The backticks format the compliance configuration key as Markdown inline code. The parenthetical values are compliance frameworks, with no shell execution behavior.

content.value_statement: Complex features require coordinated decisions across data, APIs, interfaces, tests, and operations. This skill organizes delivery into connected phases with clear outputs and validation.
actual_capabilities: Plans database, backend, and frontend architecture in a dependency-aware sequence.
Defines API contracts before coordinating backend and frontend implementation.
Organizes backend, frontend, and database implementation tasks for parallel delivery.
Specifies contract, integration, end-to-end, load, and visual regression testing.
Includes security review, deployment infrastructure, observability, and performance optimization phases.
Accepts stack, deployment, feature flag, API, testing, and compliance preferences.
limitations: It provides orchestration instructions, not a standalone executable workflow.
Named subagent types require compatible Task tool support or manual adaptation.
Generated implementations still require environment-specific testing, permissions, and expert review.
The referenced detailed implementation playbook is not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product Feature
use_cases.description: Create a phased delivery plan that connects schemas, APIs, interfaces, tests, and deployment requirements.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Implementation
use_cases.description: Divide approved architecture into backend, frontend, and database work that converges through shared contracts.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Production Rollout
use_cases.description: Add security, infrastructure, observability, performance, feature flags, and rollback planning before release.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Feature Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a full-stack feature for [goal]. Use [stack], identify missing requirements, and define outputs for each delivery phase.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a structured plan for a clearly described feature.

prompt_templates.title: Design Contracts and Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the database, API contract, backend services, and frontend components for [feature]. Include authentication, validation, accessibility, and migration requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn approved requirements into connected architecture decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Implementation and Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Orchestrate implementation of [feature] across backend, frontend, and database work. Define contract, integration, end-to-end, load, and security tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate parallel implementation while preserving contract traceability.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Advanced Production Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare [feature] for [deployment target] under [compliance standard]. Include CI/CD gates, observability, performance targets, feature flags, rollback, and ownership.
prompt_templates.scenario: Develop a production readiness plan with operational and compliance constraints.

output_examples.input: Plan a customer notification preferences feature using React, FastAPI, and PostgreSQL.
output: Architecture phase: define preference entities, consent history, API contracts, authorization rules, and accessible interface states.
Implementation phase: coordinate migrations, service endpoints, React settings components, validation, logging, and tracing.
Validation phase: test contracts, consent enforcement, error states, responsive behavior, performance, and rollback procedures.

output_examples.input: Prepare an existing billing dashboard for a controlled AWS rollout.
output: Release plan: package services, define infrastructure, add automated quality gates, and configure a staged feature flag.
Operations plan: establish service indicators, dashboards, alerts, correlation identifiers, and an accountable rollback procedure.
Readiness checks: verify authorization, payment-data handling, browser journeys, load targets, and zero-downtime deployment.

output_examples.input: Design API-first delivery for a GraphQL inventory reservation feature.
output: Define reservation consistency rules, schema changes, GraphQL operations, authorization boundaries, and conflict responses.
Generate aligned backend, frontend, and database workstreams from the approved contract.
Validate consumer compatibility, concurrent reservations, failure recovery, monitoring, and release controls.

best_practices: Resolve requirements, constraints, ownership, and success metrics before starting architecture.
Keep database, API, frontend, and test artifacts traceable to the same approved requirements.
Verify security, performance, observability, and rollback behavior in the target environment before release.
anti_patterns: Do not begin parallel implementation before approving shared data and API contracts.
Do not treat generated infrastructure or security guidance as validated production configuration.
Do not declare completion without contract tests, critical user journeys, monitoring, and rollback evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill implement the feature automatically?
faq.answer: It guides agents through implementation phases. Actual changes depend on available tools, repository context, permissions, and user approval.

faq.question: Which technology stacks can it support?
faq.answer: The workflow is stack-configurable and gives examples for React, Next.js, FastAPI, Django, Node.js, Go, PostgreSQL, and MongoDB.

faq.question: Does it require multiple agents?
faq.answer: The instructions reference specialized Task tool subagents. You can adapt the same phases for one capable agent when those subagents are unavailable.

faq.question: What testing does the workflow cover?
faq.answer: It covers unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, load, visual regression, accessibility, security, and performance validation.

faq.question: Can it deploy directly to production?
faq.answer: It can guide deployment configuration and rollout planning. Production execution still requires valid credentials, approvals, target-specific checks, and rollback readiness.

faq.question: How should teams handle compliance requirements?
faq.answer: Specify the required framework before planning. Qualified reviewers must validate generated controls and evidence against the real environment.
